newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline prices end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline prices end sharply higher.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline prices ended Tuesday sharply higher, with crude and heating oil pushed up to a lesser extent, on a combination of bullish political news and refineries cutting operating rates.

"Gasoline clearly was the leader here unlike every other day, while heating oil and crude lagged," said Smith Barney analyst John Saucer, noting gasoline has trailed recent gains in crude and heating oil.
October gasoline ended 2.76 cents a gallon higher at 62.83 cents while October heating oil settled up 2.21 cents a gallon to 69.69 cents.
November crude oil settled 70 cents higher at $24.07 a barrel. The October contract in crude expired last Friday.
"Earlier we had heard about refineries cutting back on their runs, and things strengthened in the cash market," said a trader.
The gasoline spot market firmed on news Coastal Corp shut its 20,000 barrel per day catalytic cracking unit in Corpus Christi, Texas last Friday for maintenance.
In Coffeyville, Kansas, Farmland Industries Inc took down a catalytic cracker at its refinery there for at least 10 days.

On the political front, doctors are set to decide Wednesday when they will operate on the heart of Russia's President Boris Yeltin. The market fears Yeltsin's ailing health could create political instability in the region. Russia is one of the world's largest oil producers.

In the oil-rich Middle East, General Mohsen Rezaei, commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, was quoted in the daily Tehran Times as saying Tehran would strongly retaliate throughout the Gulf against any aggressive moves by the United States or Israel.
Dealers said, however, that Tuesday's political news provided a bullish backdrop rather than any substantial fundamental support.
"Yeltsin's health is not going to affect Russia's (oil) exports," said a trader.

Analysts said weakness in gasoline prices in the past month had created a bottom, and they expected gasoline prices to stabilize around Tuesday's levels. Several analysts shrugged off talk of imminent gasoline imports from Europe, which last week created oversupply concerns.
"Gasoline prices are very likely stabilizing here. The imports are such a small amount of the total picture," said Thomas Blakeslee of Cargill Investor Services.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
